jobs.occupation: Siemens Energy Graduate Program – Program Manager Operational Excellence (m/f/d) (Projektleiter/in)
jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Whether you’re a recent graduate or have a few years of experience, you are the future of innovation and leadership. That’s why the global Siemens Energy Graduate Program can help you unleash your full potential. With guidance from experienced mentors, extensive training opportunities, and the chance to expand your global network, you will grow both your career and your personal capabilities.

What You Can Expect

(DEL: :DEL)

Over two exciting years, you’ll gain hands-on experiences and become an active part of your team’s daily activities. Through impactful projects in three customized assignments - including an eight-month international placement - you’ll gain a deep understanding of Siemens Energy. A dedicated mentor will support you every step of the way, giving you the chance to explore different roles, engage in immersive experiences, and build a strong network with peers and industry leaders.

As part of the Operational Excellence team, you will support and drive strategic and operational initiatives that enhance productivity, foster a culture of continuous improvement, and deliver measurable waste reduction.

How You’ll Make an Impact

As part of our Graduate Program, you are on the Siemens Energy team. You’ll share our purpose in energizing society by supporting customers with transitioning to a more sustainable world and work on real global issues, creating solutions that directly make an impact.
* Drive strategic and operational excellence initiatives as an internal project manager, supporting priority topics across the organization and translating strategy into execution
* Support Lean and continuous improvement initiatives by contributing to value stream mappings, identifying inefficiencies, and helping teams implement concrete improvement measures
* Prepare and facilitate workshops, working sessions, or project meetings to structure complex topics, align stakeholders and enable collaborative, action-oriented outcomes
* Support the development of concepts, frameworks or pilots in areas such as productivity, ways of working and continuous improvement culture

What You Bring
* Strong interest in operational excellence, organizational development, lean and transformation topics
* Relevant experience through internships and/or working student roles is essential; additional permanent work experience of up to 36 months is welcome
* A master's or doctoral degree in engineering, business administration or a related field
* Minimum of 3 months of international experience gained through studying or working
* Excellent English skills to engage in a multicultural environment, with flexibility and willingness for international travel

Grid Technologies

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Siemens Energy Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by at least 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Recruitment Process 

We undertake a detailed selection process comprising the following stages: CV screening, test assessment, video interview, and a final panel interview. You’ll receive the necessary details ahead of each stage as you progress!

Siemens Energy Graduate Program Website: https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/company/jobs/graduate-program.html

jobs.occupation: Offshore HVDC Site Coordinator / Electrical Supervisor (Ingenieur/in - Elektrotechnik)
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Electrical Supervisor to support offshore HVDC converter platform activities, covering maintenance, troubleshooting, commissioning, and site coordination. The role combines technical oversight, contractor management, electrical safety leadership, and interface coordination within a complex offshore energy environment. Candidates with HVDC, offshore wind, or high-voltage infrastructure experience are highly preferred.

Your Tasks

- Coordinate and supervise maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and commissioning activities on offshore HVDC converter platforms.
- Manage OEMs, contractors, and service providers while ensuring efficient execution of offshore works.
- Ensure compliance with HSE requirements, Permit-to-Work systems, LOTO procedures, and electrical safety standards.
- Monitor work progress, technical quality, schedule adherence, and compliance with project requirements.
- Coordinate interfaces between operations, engineering, commissioning, HSE teams, and contractors.
- Track technical defects, non-conformities, and outstanding works while preparing site reports and escalating critical issues.
- Assume VEFK (Responsible Electrical Person) duties where formally appointed.

Your qualifications

- Technician, Master Craftsman, or equivalent qualification in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Experience within offshore wind, HVDC/HGÜ systems, substations, high-voltage installations, or energy infrastructure projects.
- Strong knowledge of HV/MV equipment, electrical isolation procedures, LOTO, and Permit-to-Work systems.
- Experience in site supervision, contractor coordination, maintenance, and/or commissioning activities.
- VEFK qualification or solid experience within the German electrical safety framework is highly desirable.
- Good understanding of HVDC converter systems and reactive power compensation systems is an advantage.
- Strong HSE mindset, proactive approach, and ability to work independently.
- Good English skills; German language skills are considered beneficial.
- Willingness to work offshore, travel regularly, and participate in standby rotations.
- Offshore medical fitness and offshore safety certification (or willingness to obtain them).

jobs.description:
Create your own happiness!

Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?

Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?

What you can look forward to…

The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.

We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position, but a reduction in hours is possible. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term due to parental leave, but an extension is possible.

Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.

The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.

We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.

Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the infants entrusted to us in accordance with our educational philosophy, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. Your would spend your daily life spekaing English.

You would be a permanent member of the nursery team. Some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.

Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.

We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.

The Team: One for all, all for one!

Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.

On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.

Has this piqued your curiosity? Then be sure to read on…

Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.

To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.

We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.

Feel free to get to know us!

The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.

The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).

There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 46 children are currently cared for by eight early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.

The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.

We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…

Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.

Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.

Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.

As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.

The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?

Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.

If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).

Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

jobs.occupation: System Engineer for Science and Planetary Defence Missions (m/f/d) (Ingenieur/in - Systems Engineering)
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

As a System Engineer Predevelopment you will play a key role in shaping the earliest phases of cutting‑edge satellite missions. In this role, you will lead platform‑level system engineering activities during Phase A/B1, orchestrate technical inputs from expert teams and subcontractors, and help define the mission and system architecture. You will contribute to laying the technical, programmatic, and schedule foundations that ensure mission success through the entire development lifecycle.

Tasks:

- Support the Lead System Engineer for the Phase A/B1 study.
- Coordinate technical inputs from specialist engineering departments and individual subcontractors.
- Execute trade‑offs and analyses to define the mission and system architecture.
- Lead the parts of the platform and subsystem system design as an architect, including deriving and maintaining requirements from satellite to subsystem level.
- Support Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) activities for the mission.
- Contribute to the assessment of the satellite development approach to ensure the target Technology Readiness Level (TRL) by the end of Phase B1.
- Support the definition of the overall project breakdown structure (Work Breakdown Structure) for phases B2, C/D, and E1 through in‑orbit commissioning.
- Assist in developing the programme plan for the satellite across phases B2, C/D, and E1 up to in‑orbit calibration and validation.
- Support the creation of a project implementation schedule for the platform, aligned with the overall programme planning.
Analyse and assess potential cost drivers for the platform.
- Support the identification and evaluation of technical and programmatic risks, including cost, schedule, and feasibility drivers.
- Support the definition and implementation of risk mitigation measures for the platform.
Your Qualifications

Minimum:

- Master-level degree in aerospace engineering with a focus on space systems
- Knowledge of science, exploration and space safety space missions
- Competencies in space mission design, satellite systems engineering and spacecraft subsystem design
- High level of flexibility, willingness to work in international teams and ability to keep tight schedules
- High motivation, pro-active working approach and strong sense of responsibility
- Excellent communication, presentation and documentation skills
- Fluency in both spoken and written (business) English

Ideal:

- Industry experience in space system engineering
- Knowledge of requirements engineering for subsystems of space systems and preparation of specifications
- Experience in Model Based Systems Engineering
- Fluency in German language

jobs.description:
...you're in the middle of it

The Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at Goethe University Frankfurt is seeking a PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher to join the research group of Dr. Hahnefeld. The successful candidate will contribute to an interdisciplinary research project in cooperation with the Fraunhofer ITMP Frankfurt at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipid biology and inflammation research.

The project investigates how lipid metabolism and lipid-mediated signaling are regulated in inflammatory settings. The work combines cell-based experiments with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and targeted lipid mediator measurements. A particular focus will be placed on the development, optimization and application of robust analytical and computational workflows for the analysis of complex biological datasets. The research group uses high-resolution mass spectrometry and reproducible bioinformatic approaches to investigate lipid-mediated mechanisms in inflammatory and metabolic diseases. The position offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment with interdisciplinary partners in lipid biology, immunology, imaging and proteomics.

The position is limited up to three years.

Your Role:

- Plan, conduct and document experiments in cellular models of inflammation and metabolic perturbation.
- Prepare biological samples and perform LC-HRMS-based lipidomics and metabolomics measurements and further develop associated analytical workflows.
- Perform GC-HRMS-based analysis of fatty acids
- Conduct LC-MS/MS measurements of lipid mediators using established methods.
- Perform comprehensive quality control, raw-data validation, data annotation and statistical analysis of complex mass spectrometry datasets.
- Develop and apply reproducible workflows for data processing, visualization and interpretation using R and/or Python.
- Contribute to the integration and interpretation of lipidomics data with complementary datasets generated by collaborating groups, including imaging- and proteomics-based data.
- Validate selected findings in close collaboration with project partners.
- Present research results in scientific publications, project meetings and at national and international conferences.

... your skills are what we're looking for

- A completed Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in analytical chemistry, chemistry, pharmacy, biochemistry, molecular life sciences or a related discipline.
- A strong theoretical and practical background in analytical chemistry.
- Practical experience with liquid chromatography, gas chromatography and mass spectrometry is desirable.
- Experience with high-resolution mass spectrometry, lipidomics, metabolomics, method development or biological sample preparation is advantageous but not necessary.
- Experience in cell culture, molecular or cellular biology is advantageous.
- Knowledge of statistical data analysis and programming in R and/or Python, or a strong willingness to acquire these skills.
- A careful, structured and independent working style, combined with reliability and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team.
- Very good written and spoken English skills.
- Due to legal regulations, valid proof of measles immunity / measles vaccination is required

- An interdisciplinary doctoral research project at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipidomics and inflammation research.

Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.
About Us

The Hannover Medical School (MHH), with about 10,000 employees the biggest company of Lower Saxony, is a university institution for research and teaching in the human and dental medicine and a university hospital of supra-maximum medical care. Research, teaching, medical care and administration work hand in hand in the integration model at the MHH-campus.

The Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics (PLRI) is one of the largest university centres for medical informatics in Germany. It belongs to two leading universities, is situated in one of Europe's most research-intensive regions, and offers excellent opportunities for research. In interdisciplinary projects, the PLRI collaborates with health centres, research institutes, corporations, and public institutions in order to shape the future of the health system and medicine. The activities range from diverse topics on the local level, to regional, national, and global collaborations.

The research group "Clinical Data Science" focuses on the detection of novel routine clinical and -omics biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis to personalize and thus improve patient treatment. To achieve this, we integrate phenotypical information and routine clinical as well as (multi)-omics data by high-dimensional statistics and state-of-the-art artificial intelligence to gain novel insights into underlying disease pathomechanisms. Moreover, we are interested in developing and implementing research data platforms for complex (multi-)omics data. The project "MALDIDive: Enabling AI Research with Public MALDI-TOF Fingerprints across Microbial Diversity", to be carried out within an interdisciplinary research team and funded by the German Research Foundation, will establish a well curated data platform of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry datasets from the Leibniz Institute German Collection of Mircoorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH (DSMZ). We are looking for an enthusiastic PostDoc who is interested in omics data platform development and deployment for future AI use.

Your Responsibilities

- data platform architecture, backend, and frontend development as well as deployment for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry database/platform and associated metadata
- development of interactive data visualization concepts and their implementation into data platform
- development and realization of short explanatory videos for platform users
- co-organization and co-leading of stakeholder workshops to define user requirements and conduct user test cycles
- presentation to the scientific community, i.e., by publishing in high-level journals and via presentations at international conferences
- close collaboration with interdisciplinary project partners from AI / data science, analytical, and micro­biological research communities, particularly the DSMZ
- bachelor / master student co-supervision

Your Profile

- PhD / Dr. rer. nat. / Dr.-Ing. degree in data science / bioinformatics / computational biology / informatics / physics or similar research fields
- expertise in the work on databases, interactive platform development, -omics and biomedical data, and / or artificial intelligence / machine learning
- proficiency in backend / frontend development and / or database programming, including one or more of the following programming languages: VueJS, TypeScript, SQL, PYTHON, R Shiny, nginx, Docker, etc.
- proficiency in English (written and oral)
- desired: experience with code documentary systems and RestAPI
- desired: knowledge of the German language

We offer

- a full-time position initially limited to two years with 38.5 hours per week at one of the largest employers in the state of Lower Saxony
- depending on your individual qualifications, a salary according to TV-L salary group E13 is possible, with the benefits associated with public sector employment (e.g. occupational pension scheme and supplementary insurance through VBL)
- an exciting role at the interface of research, healthcare and science management
- a supportive induction process within a motivated and interdisciplinary team
- support to pursue postdoctoral career (e.g., mentoring programs, etc.)
- working in a highly motivated and cooperative research team of scientists
- excellent perspectives for your scientific career development and networking
- individual training and further education opportunities
- a comprehensive company health management - because your health is important to us

jobs.description:
Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:

Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project

(Full-Time / Part-Time)

Location: Frankfurt
Employment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are available
Type of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 years
Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.

The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.

Your tasks

- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.
- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.
- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.
- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.
- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.
- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.
- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.

Your profile

- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.
- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).
- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.
- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.
- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).
- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).
- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.
- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.
- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.
- Very good command of English.
- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).

Desirable skills

- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles
- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)
- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projects

We offer

- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.

Contact

Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung
Senckenberganlage 25
60325 Frankfurt am Main

For specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de

The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow . The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will contribute to and consult on developing a web-based open-access tool on Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) for reproducible data and modelling workflows and transform biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation.

Your tasks

- Design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform: a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) over the full GBIF corpus (~3.9 billion occurrence records) and OBIS (~207 million records).
- Architect and operate the hybrid setup with the AWS side (S3 data lake, elastic batch compute, optional GPU profile), working with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, tiles, API) in cooperation with central IT.
- Build the batch pipelines: monthly full-corpus rebuild, per-species extraction and SDM training jobs; workflow orchestration (Nextflow/Snakemake), containerisation.
- Build an H3-based aggregation and map-tile generation pipeline.
- Manage cloud costs, infrastructure documentation and handover.
- Advise the project team on infrastructure and hosting decisions.

Your profile

- Several years of professional experience designing and operating cloud data platforms (AWS: S3, Batch, Spot Instances; infrastructure as code).
- Hands-on experience with columnar / lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Spark or Dask) on datasets in the billion-record range.
- Strong PostgreSQL, including PostGIS.
- Experience with large-scale geospatial processing: spatial indexing (e.g. H3 hexagonal grids) and map-tile pipelines.
- Experience working with biodiversity occurrence data (GBIF, OBIS) and environmental layers (e.g. Bio-ORACLE).
- Knowledge of Python, Docker, Git/CI.
- Very good command of English.

Desirable skills

- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest).
- A track record in reproducible scientific computing or open-source projects.

- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
